project.name: fambam
project.description: A private, family-centred photo and memory platform for international relatives who want to share and preserve photographs without relying on mainstream social media.

git_tagging.definition: Git tags map directly onto PROJECT_ROADMAP.md / docs/IMPLEMENTATION_GUIDE.md identifiers. <n> is the roadmap phase number (Phase P<n> -> phase-<n>) and <NN> is the roadmap stage number within that phase (FPA-P<n>-S<NN> -> phase-<n>-s<NN>). ADR numbers never determine git phase numbers. This matches the convention documented and used in the sibling dolved project.
tagging_rules: Only a completed planned roadmap stage receives a phase-<n>-s<NN> tag.
Intermediate commits made while a stage is still in progress receive no stage tag.
The stage tag is applied to the single commit that completes the planned roadmap stage.
If a stage's entire scope is accepting an ADR, the ADR-acceptance commit is that stage's completion commit and receives the tag directly.
Otherwise, an ADR-acceptance commit remains untagged until the authorised implementation stage that follows it is itself completed and accepted.
phase-<n> (no stage suffix) is created only once, on the commit that completes that phase's final stage and passes the phase's full acceptance gate.
git_tagging.roadmap_relationship: PROJECT_ROADMAP.md phase identifiers (P##) and docs/IMPLEMENTATION_GUIDE.md stage identifiers (FPA-P##-S##) are the direct source of the tag numbers -- this is the same numbering, not a parallel scheme. The delivery_log array (top level of this file) records every tag actually produced, mapped to its roadmap stage.

completion_rules: tasks.json is advanced in the same commit.
The commit remains within the agreed stage boundary.

stages.title: Add baseline observability

The synthetic consumer's message-receive logic was also extracted into a tested function, removing an unhandled-IndexError risk on an empty poll.

stages.title: Harden account security
notes: Shared session and remember-token revocation, operator account revocation, password policy and safeguarded HIBP screening, reset throttling, optional TOTP and frontend account-security surfaces were committed locally on 2026-08-03 before the delayed independent review completed; the premature local completion tags were removed and the stage returned to in-progress pending correction.

An independent review found two blocking issues (a revoked account could complete an already-pending two-factor challenge; bcrypt silently truncated passwords beyond 72 bytes) and several important findings (repeatable plaintext recovery-code disclosure, unattributed operator revocation, a login timing side-channel distinguishing unknown/revoked accounts, an insecure local secure-cookie example default). Codex corrected every finding; a focused independent re-review verified each fix directly against the code, the full test suite and a live reproduction of the original revoked-mid-challenge exploit, confirming it is now rejected.
FPA-P02-S04 and the Phase 2 acceptance gate passed and were completed on the same commit on 2026-08-03.

stages.title: Accept family spaces and tenancy ADR
notes: ADR-0005 accepted 2026-08-03 (git tag phase-3-s01). Stage scope was solely ADR acceptance, so the ADR commit is the stage-completion commit.

Tenant model: family_spaces + family_space_memberships (ULID identifiers, mutable presentation slug); all five roadmap-named roles with a Phase 3 baseline meaning; family-space creation as a narrow platform-level capability (users.can_create_family_spaces) never implied by any membership role and never auto-granted at bootstrap; one invitation domain covering new-account and existing-account joins with atomic, race-safe rejoin for previously removed members; friendly-URL resolution where unknown and inaccessible tenants are structurally indistinguishable (both 404); at least one active Owner per space enforced at both the application and database-trigger layers; PostgreSQL RLS treated as three distinct policy classes (tenant registry, access-control table, ordinary tenant-owned content tables) rather than one generic policy, to avoid a circular dependency between tenant resolution and tenant-scoped access control.

The ADR intentionally records trust boundaries and required guarantees rather than a frozen PostgreSQL implementation; exact policy composition and session-context mechanics are left to Phase 3 implementation, verified against the ADR's stated guarantees.

stages.title: Implement family spaces and memberships
notes: Family Space and membership foundations, capability-gated creation, Owner safeguards, family-scoped invitations and atomic membership reactivation were implemented and verified against SQLite and PostgreSQL 17.6.

The approved persistent migration created the fallback Family Archive, assigned the first account as Owner and other accounts as Members, associated historical invitations, expired pending Phase 2 invitations, removed their claims and retired can_invite.
The complete repository gate passed before review approval and stage completion on 2026-08-04 (git tag phase-3-s02).

stages.title: Implement route context, policies and explicit scoping

React Router now provides the protected URL-derived Family Space route; tenant-aware TanStack Query keys and nested invitation endpoints keep frontend server state aligned with the active slug.
The complete repository gate and rebuilt-stack HTTP checks passed before review approval and stage completion on 2026-08-04 (git tag phase-3-s03).

stages.title: Add PostgreSQL row-level security

The ordinary tenant-table USING/WITH CHECK pattern was documented and verified without introducing speculative production schema; PostgreSQL 17.6 integration tests directly proved non-recursive registry resolution, fail-closed reads and writes, atomic authoritative flows and context cleanup.

The complete repository gate, approved persistent migration and rebuilt-stack role, policy, data-preservation, HTTP, infrastructure and observability checks passed before stage completion on 2026-08-04 (git tag phase-3-s04).

stages.title: Add tenancy audit and deletion foundations

The accepted review follow-up added direct PostgreSQL concurrency, multi-space cross-tenant and insert-only audit-boundary proof, plus frontend protected-route, cache-isolation and membership-loss regressions.

The complete repository gate, PostgreSQL 17.6 integration suite and rebuilt-stack infrastructure and observability smokes passed before FPA-P03-S05 and Phase 3 completion on 2026-08-04 (git tags phase-3-s05 and phase-3).

stages.title: Accept people, accounts and relationships ADR
notes: ADR-0006 accepted 2026-08-05 (git tag phase-4-s01). Stage scope was solely ADR acceptance, so the ADR-acceptance commit is the stage-completion commit. Person identity is Family-Space-local with no cross-tenant identity bridge or matching; an immutable ULID Person identity carries mutable names, a shared uncertain-date concept for birth/death information, a deceased-state fact composed independently of date-uncertainty, and biography/notes as shared archival content under whole-record visibility. A single proposed-versus-authoritative distinction applies uniformly to Person details and relationships -- Members may contribute or propose, Owner/Administrator confirm, replace, remove or resolve as authoritative -- with proposed relationships excluded from the authoritative graph until approved and approval re-validating against current state. One-to-one User-to-Person linking per Family Space allows Member and reachable-Contributor self-claim proposals subject to Owner/Administrator approval, with Guest excluded. Relationships use one canonical edge per concept with derived inverse wording from a fixed, additive vocabulary and never grant permission. Family Circles are a real, flat, People-only, presentation-only construct barred from ever being consulted by authorization, policy or RLS. The Phase 4 visibility baseline gives Owner/Administrator/Member default Person-directory access and gives Contributor/Guest none, as an explicit placeholder for Phase 5/6/7's resource-grant model. Person, link, relationship, circle and circle-membership tables inherit ADR-0005's Class C tenant-owned-table guarantees, with no RLS SQL frozen in the ADR. Person merge uses a redirect/tombstone record with atomic reconciliation of Phase-4-owned references, structured merge provenance distinct from ordinary AuditEvents, and reversal bounded to what Phase 4 itself can unambiguously restore. Person detail routes use the immutable ULID with no Person slug, and User-to-Person links survive account revocation and membership removal, changed only by an explicit, audited Owner/Administrator unlink or correction.

stages.title: Implement person records
notes: Family-Space-local ULID Person records, normalized uncertain dates, independent deceased state, bounded biography, provisional Member contributions, Owner/Administrator authoritative writes and proposal review, whole-record role visibility, tenant-aware audits, Class C forced RLS and a feature-oriented TanStack Query frontend were implemented and verified on 2026-08-06.

stages.title: Link accounts to people
notes: One-to-one Family-Space account links, bounded Member self-claims with the future reachable-Contributor ceiling preserved without treating a guessed ULID as reachability, Owner/Administrator approval/correction/removal, access-loss retention, tenant-aware audits, forced Class C RLS and a typed TanStack Query Person-page flow were implemented and verified on 2026-08-06.

stages.title: Implement relationships and family circles
notes: Canonical directed/symmetric relationship edges with derived inverse wording, a fixed additive vocabulary, deterministic lock-and-validate writes, separate Member proposals with current-state Owner/Administrator approval, flat People-only presentation Circles, distinct audits, forced Class C RLS and typed tenant-aware TanStack Query frontend flows were implemented and verified on 2026-08-06.

stages.title: Implement person merge and correction workflow

stages.title: Accept media storage and upload pipeline ADR
notes: ADR-0007 accepted 2026-08-10 (git tag phase-5-s01). Stage scope was solely ADR acceptance, so the ADR-acceptance commit is the stage-completion commit. Phase 5 owns Family-Space-local MediaUpload and MediaVariant infrastructure without introducing the Phase 6 Photo domain. Direct browser uploads receive bounded authority for an extension-independent tenant staging key; server-side validation detects the format before write-once-equivalent finalisation under archival or quarantine keys, and racing or reused authority must not replace preserved bytes. The state machine separates arrived-but-untrusted uploads from SHA-256-verified immutable originals; deterministic Laravel jobs perform validation, required configurable malware scanning, complete original metadata preservation, canonical generation and fixed presentation variants for JPEG, PNG, HEIC/HEIF, WebP and TIFF. Ordinary APIs and presentation assets withhold privacy-sensitive metadata, while authorised Owner/Administrator/Member original downloads deliberately return the untouched original. Signed original access records original_download_authorised rather than claiming an unobserved object-storage GET. Contributor upload remains an explicit Phase 6/7 resource-scoped placeholder, not a permanent prohibition. ADR-0005 tenant teardown is the sole deletion exception for preserved Phase 5 media, and bulk upload remains independent per-file work grouped only for presentation.

stages.title: Implement upload initiation and completion
notes: Implemented MediaUpload persistence and Class C tenant RLS; Owner, Administrator and Member initiation; Contributor/Guest Phase 5 deferral; per-tenant/uploader idempotency with request-fingerprint conflict rejection; extension-independent staging keys; a browser-reachable, key-scoped 15-minute PUT authority with signed If-None-Match write-once enforcement; independently inspected and conditionally idempotent initiated-to-uploaded completion; retained tenant/correlation/trace context; upload-initiation auditing; configurable 100 MiB completion ceiling; LocalStack CORS; and a typed feature-local TanStack Query upload flow. Validation, scanning, detected-format archival finalisation and processing remain FPA-P05-S03 or later.

stages.title: Validate and preserve originals
notes: Implemented unique tenant-aware validation jobs; signature-derived JPEG, PNG, HEIC/HEIF, WebP and TIFF detection; AVIF/unknown rejection; bounded ImageMagick decode and pixel limits; server-computed SHA-256; replaceable fail-closed ClamAV scanning; write-once archival/quarantine finalisation with conditional S3 writes and collision proof; durable accepted/quarantined transitions, audits and staging cleanup; a narrowly discoverable, unique-job-based seven-day quarantine purge that retains rejection rows; persistent migrations; real LocalStack, decoder and EICAR smoke coverage; and PostgreSQL Class C verification. Metadata extraction, canonical assets and presentation variants remain FPA-P05-S04 or later.

stages.title: Extract metadata and generate canonical assets
notes: Implemented a unique tenant-aware canonical job keyed by the frozen source SHA-256; source integrity re-verification; replaceable ExifTool extraction of dimensions, orientation, camera data, technical capture timestamp, GPS and losslessly base64-encoded raw EXIF/ICC profiles; strict ordinary-response withholding of private metadata; bounded ImageMagick auto-orientation, sRGB normalization and complete metadata stripping; deterministic write-once JPEG or alpha-preserving PNG canonical finalisation; and the preserved-to-processing transition. Real HEIC, HEIF, TIFF, orientation, alpha, stripping and deterministic-regeneration coverage and PostgreSQL Class C private-metadata verification passed. Variants remain FPA-P05-S05.

stages.title: Generate presentation variants
notes: Implemented a fixed centrally-defined V1 thumbnail/card/display vocabulary; metadata-stripped sRGB WebP generation from the canonical; versioned MediaVariant identity and tenant storage keys; unique canonical-integrity-bound jobs; write-once and database idempotency; processing-to-ready/degraded transitions; safe regeneration of disposable variants; persistent migration; real deterministic ImageMagick coverage; and PostgreSQL Class C verification. Secure delivery remains FPA-P05-S06.

stages.title: Secure media delivery
notes: Implemented tenant- and role-authorized canonical, current-version variant and preserved-original authority endpoints; five-minute key-scoped signed GETs capped at fifteen minutes; verified response MIME types and Range support; explicit private-bucket, CORS and signature-validation controls; fail-closed unavailable/cross-tenant behaviour; and truthful original_download_authorised auditing without claiming an unobserved download. Real LocalStack and role/state/audit regression coverage passed. Recovery, bulk upload and tenant media teardown remain FPA-P05-S07.

stages.title: Add upload recovery and bulk upload
notes: Implemented source-bound duplicate-safe degraded recovery; independent per-file bulk upload grouped by an uploader-scoped batch ULID; typed TanStack Query batch mutation/polling with accessible partial-failure reporting; a narrowly executable PostgreSQL scheduler sweep and unique tenant-aware jobs for the configurable 24-hour abandoned-upload cutoff; retryable staging cleanup; and idempotent Family Space media-prefix and Phase-5-row teardown. Persistent migration, PostgreSQL cross-tenant discovery, role/privacy regressions, frontend batch coverage and real LocalStack tenant-prefix cleanup passed on 2026-08-10. No Phase 6 Photo domain or standalone media deletion was introduced.

stages.title: Accept photo domain, provenance and organisation ADR
notes: ADR-0008 accepted 2026-08-24 (git tag phase-6-s01). Stage scope was solely ADR acceptance, so the ADR-acceptance commit is the stage-completion commit. Photo.media_upload_id is required and unique, one-directional to MediaUpload, with at most one Photo per MediaUpload; a ready MediaUpload may exist indefinitely without becoming a Photo. Photo.created_by (distinct from MediaUpload.user_id) identifies who created the Photo record and is authority-bearing for later contribution, visibility and deletion rules. Photographer, scanner and original physical owner are single-valued Person-or-mutually-exclusive-free-text provenance roles following ADR-0006's Member-proposes/Owner-or-Administrator-confirms pattern; the physical-owner free-text field is named physical_source_description, never source_album. Historical date reuses ADR-0006's uncertain-date concept and stays strictly separate from MediaUpload's EXIF capture timestamp. PhotoPerson (FPA-P06-S03) uses the same proposed/authoritative pattern, and only confirmed rows are authoritative human ground truth that later machine recognition (Phase 9/10) may never overwrite. Photo.visibility has exactly two values, family_space and private; selected-audience sharing lives entirely in Albums via AlbumGrant (can_view/can_contribute), never a parallel photo_grants system. Adding a private Photo to a broader Album is an explicit, authorized, UI-visible, tested widening operation; removing it from every such Album automatically restores exactly its intrinsic visibility, computed from live state. Default family_space Album contribution is fixed product policy: Owner, Administrator, the Album's creator and ordinary Member all contribute by default; Contributor only through an explicit AlbumGrant; Guest never. This is Contributor's first concrete resource-scoped grant. Phase 5's MediaUploadPolicy delivery endpoints must become Photo/Album-aware once a MediaUpload is attached to a Photo, so the existing MediaUpload ULID can never bypass private/restricted access. Photo deletion is reversible soft deletion only, authorised for Owner/Administrator on any Photo and for the creator on their own while they retain Family Space access; Phase 5 assets and associated Album/story/comment/reaction rows are never affected. Stories and comments are author-editable with Owner/Administrator moderation authority; reactions use a small fixed vocabulary with no ranking or engagement-feed use. Dynamic views remain query-only; persisted views remain Phase 11. Duplicate linkage, Event/Event-Album structure, machine face data and persisted dynamic views are explicitly out of scope for Phase 6.

Amended 2026-08-24 (same-day pre-implementation reconciliation, ADR text updated in place, no new tag): split the conflated physical_source_description field into an identity-bearing original-physical-owner claim (propose/confirm) and an ordinary archive_source_description field (Member-editable, no approval); moved Photo-visibility delivery enforcement from FPA-P06-S04 into FPA-P06-S02 so MediaUploadPolicy respects Photo.visibility as soon as the column exists, closing a temporary bypass window; added a human-supplied location field (free text, propose/confirm, distinct from Phase 5 GPS) implemented in FPA-P06-S03; added Family-Space-scoped free-text Photo tags with no approval workflow, implemented in FPA-P06-S02; fixed AlbumGrant's can_contribute-implies-can_view invariant; explicitly differentiated Private (zero AlbumGrant rows) from Selected (grant-governed) Album visibility; confirmed AlbumGrant survives ADR-0005's in-place membership reactivation with no extra reconciliation; clarified that AlbumGrant governs presentation access only and never confers preserved-original download, which continues to follow ADR-0007's role policy against the Photo's own intrinsic visibility; fixed Contributor's upload path as strictly Album-scoped via AlbumGrant.can_contribute, with the resulting Photo created already attached to that Album and defaulting to private rather than family_space visibility; corrected implementation-guide wording that suggested a permanent-deletion path, which Phase 6 does not build; fixed new-Photo default visibility as family_space; and fixed Photo-creation authority (Member from their own upload only, Owner/Administrator from any upload, Contributor only via scoped Album contribution). No architectural decision was reversed.

stages.title: Accept events and collaborative sharing ADR
notes: ADR-0009 accepted 2026-08-25 (git tag phase-7-s01). Stage scope was solely ADR acceptance, so the ADR-acceptance commit is the stage-completion commit. Event is a Family-Space-owned resource with presentation-only status, Member/Owner/Administrator creation, creator-or-administrator editing, Owner/Administrator soft deletion and no visibility enum. Album.event_id and Photo.primary_event_id are nullable, single-Event organisational references introduced before they gain any Guest authorization effect. Attendance is derived from confirmed PhotoPerson associations, never maintained separately. Event invitations deterministically reuse an existing membership without role mutation, while event_admissions has one audited, revocable and re-admittable row per Event/membership with live-computed validity. Guest authority requires a valid Event admission plus Album guest_participation or an Event-scoped AlbumGrant; non-Event Guest access remains denied. Event Guests may comment/react and may download originals at view/contribute participation, but may not author PhotoStory content. Event removal is reversible and preserves all references; duplicate review remains advisory and human-resolved. Anonymous contribution, RSVP state, automatic Guest cleanup/promotion and Event hard deletion remain out of scope.

stages.title: Implement events and event albums
notes: Completed 2026-08-25: implemented tenant-isolated Events with presentation-only status and creator/manager editing; nullable authorization-inert Album.event_id and Photo.primary_event_id references; confirmed-PhotoPerson-derived attendance and Person reverse lookup; deterministic advisory duplicate candidates; Event and Event-Album TanStack Query UI; persistent PostgreSQL migration; and focused authorization, cross-tenant, database-constraint and RLS verification.

stages.title: Implement event contributions
notes: Completed 2026-08-25: verified that Event Albums reuse ADR-0008's existing Member default-contribution and Contributor AlbumGrant.can_contribute paths unchanged, including MediaUpload.target_album_id finalisation to one private attached Photo; added focused backend and frontend regression coverage without introducing any FPA-P07-S04 Guest admission or participation behavior.

stages.title: Implement restricted guest upload links
notes: Completed 2026-08-25: added live, revocable and re-admittable EventAdmission state; Event-scoped invitations that reuse active memberships without role mutation; Album guest_participation; the narrow Guest Event/Album/Photo/media authorization exception; scoped original download; Guest comment/reaction with Story denial; Guest exclusion from ordinary Family Space and membership surfaces; reversible Event removal/restoration; typed Event admission and scoped Album UI; and required SQLite, PostgreSQL and frontend regressions. The admission lifetime is configurable through EVENT_ADMISSION_LIFETIME_DAYS with a 30-day default and no expiry sweep.

stages.title: Implement event notifications and exports
notes: Completed 2026-08-26: notifies the live Event cohort (creator, active Owner/Administrator, and memberships with a currently valid Event admission, deduplicated, uploader excluded) exactly once per Photo via a tenant-scoped per-recipient delivery ledger that resumes only unsent recipients after a partial failure. Owner/Administrator may request a bounded, overlap-protected, asynchronous curated Event archive (ZIP of untouched preserved originals plus a schema-versioned JSON manifest), with checksum-validated originals, five-minute signed downloads, 24-hour retention and hourly idempotent expiry cleanup integrated into Family Space teardown and audit. Also closed the independent Phase 7 review findings found before this stage's acceptance: Guest-created Photos no longer bypass live Event access via the Photo.created_by shortcut; concurrent new-account Event-invitation acceptance is serialized with a PostgreSQL advisory lock and deterministically reuses one account/membership; Album event detachment correctly resets guest_participation; Event updates reject every inverted date-range combination against the stored record, not only both-fields-in-one-request; event_admissions gained direct cross-tenant PostgreSQL RLS proof. No ADR-0009 correction was required.

stages.title: Accept duplicate-detection ADR
notes: ADR-0010 accepted 2026-08-26 (git tag phase-8-s01). Stage scope was solely ADR acceptance, so the ADR-acceptance commit is the stage-completion commit. Exact detection uses the existing frozen MediaUpload SHA-256 within one Family Space and discloses only Photos the actor can already view. The three-outcome choice applies to direct and asynchronous Album/Event contribution paths without changing ADR-0008 promotion authority. MediaUploadDuplicateHold pauses asynchronous promotion; DuplicateDecision durably suppresses automatic rediscovery while allowing audited Owner/Administrator reopening. New comments and reactions become Album-scoped while legacy Photo-scoped rows remain preserved and read-only. Retrospective exact candidates belong to S02; calibrated perceptual matching belongs to S03. No merge, redirect, aggregation, consolidation or automatic deletion mechanism exists.

stages.title: Implement exact duplicate detection
notes: Completed 2026-08-26: exact SHA-256 matching is tenant- and visibility-scoped across direct Photo creation and asynchronous Album/Event contribution; three-outcome resolution preserves existing promotion and contribution authority; disclosed candidate snapshots make multi-match DuplicateDecision writes deterministic under races; exact retrospective candidates, canonical pair suppression, uploader-owned duplicate holds, Album-scoped new conversation with read-only legacy preservation, persistent PostgreSQL migration, forced RLS and typed TanStack Query UI were implemented and verified. No perceptual matching or S03 calibration work was included.

stages.title: Implement perceptual similarity analysis
notes: Completed 2026-08-26: dhash-luma-64 processing version 1 with Hamming distance <= 18 produced 18 true positives, 0 false negatives, 0 false positives and 762 true negatives across the 40-asset representative local corpus. Versioned tenant-owned hashes, deterministic Laravel generation, PostgreSQL backfill discovery, exact/settled/deleted suppression, idempotent perceptual candidates, forced RLS and teardown were implemented and verified; persistent migration batch 31 and the existing-Photo backfill completed, and all private calibration copies were removed.

stages.title: Implement duplicate review
notes: Completed 2026-08-26: Owner/Administrator archive-wide review exposes exactly leave-pending or dismiss-as-not-duplicate; dismissal settles and audits the canonical pair without modifying either Photo, reopening is an audited transition on the same durable decision row, later natural detection can re-pend reopened pairs, and Members may flag only pairs of Photos they can already view. Typed feature API modules, TanStack Query hooks, accessible canonical-image comparison UI, strict Contributor/Guest exclusion and complete backend/frontend regression coverage were implemented with no merge, deletion, redirect, aggregation or consolidation mechanism.

Post-completion review closed 2026-08-27: added real PostgreSQL advisory-lock and canonical-ordering proof, Guest Event/Album hold ownership and live-authority coverage across all three choices, asynchronous invisible-match and soft-delete/restore suppression regressions, and consistent required album_id validation for new comment/reaction writes. Reopening and perceptual-threshold behavior remain unchanged; the threshold now has an explicit materially-different-source recalibration trigger.

stages.title: Build representative local benchmark
notes: Completed 2026-08-27: private, non-repository benchmark built under .local/benchmarks/face-analysis/ (anonymous B001-B038, manifest, annotations, checksum verification, contact sheets; never committed). 38 uploads inspected, all containing at least one visible face; 29 independent core scenes plus 9 repeated/format-conversion inputs; ~79 visible faces overall, 61 across the core set (10 single-face, 19 group, up to 4 faces/image). Core coverage recorded across frontal, angled/profile, small/distant, occlusion, lighting, blur, resolution, glasses, facial hair, age, grayscale and rotation conditions. Named gaps (age progression, sibling/parent resemblance, damaged scans, larger groups, heavier occlusion) are explicitly reserved for Phase 10 recognition calibration and do not block Phase 9 foundation work. Evidence reviewed and found sufficient for ADR-0011 architecture discussion; not a recognition-accuracy benchmark.

stages.title: Accept local face analysis foundation ADR
notes: ADR-0011 drafted 2026-08-27 (docs/adr/0011-local-face-analysis-foundation.md, Status: Proposed) following an architecture discussion covering provider contract shape, Laravel/Python transport and service identity, canonical-asset delivery, FaceAnalysisRun/FaceObservation persistence and identity/idempotency, embedding-storage scope (engine selection explicitly deferred to ADR-0012/FPA-P10-S02), reprocessing and invalidation, dead-letter queueing, tenancy/biometric privacy, the audit-versus-telemetry boundary, benchmark-harness discipline, and the licensing record.

Reconciled 2026-08-27 against two Codex implementation-readiness reviews: added explicit browser/service signing audiences; narrowly superseded ADR-0001's inline-first completion assumption; bounded and validated result artifacts; separated durable FaceAnalysisRun and FaceAnalysisAttempt identity; defined stale/late message, DLQ and database-state reconciliation; aligned S03-S06 ownership; named buffalo_l and recorded the licensing gate; added tenant-consistent composite relationships through MediaUpload, and required face-analysis object cleanup during Family Space teardown.

ADR-0011 accepted 2026-08-27 (git tag phase-9-s02). Stage scope was solely ADR acceptance, so the ADR-acceptance commit is the stage-completion commit. Phase 9 remains provider-neutral and inference-only on the Python side; Laravel retains all tenancy and persistence authority; canonical assets are delivered through service-audience signed URLs; bounded results use write-once transient artifacts; durable run and attempt identities make retries and unordered result queues idempotent; every biometric relationship is tenant-consistent at the database level; and clustering, identity suggestion and human review remain Phase 10 concerns.

stages.title: Implement face-analysis provider contract
notes: Completed 2026-08-27 (git tag phase-9-s03): versioned language-neutral requested/completed/failed and result-artifact contracts; a strict provider-neutral Python interface; tenant-consistent FaceAnalysisRun, FaceAnalysisAttempt and FaceObservation persistence with forced RLS; conservative fail-closed result validation; and explicit browser/service signing audiences were implemented and verified without loading a model or beginning the operational queue pipeline.

stages.title: Implement local face-analysis provider
notes: Completed 2026-08-27 (git tag phase-9-s04): pinned InsightFace 1.0.1, ONNX Runtime 1.29.0 and buffalo_l v0.7 with fail-closed full-pack checksum verification and a recorded non-commercial model-licence boundary; implemented contract-native local detection, five-point landmarks and 512-dimensional embeddings; calibrated threshold 0.6, a 4 MiB artifact ceiling and initial S05 transport settings from the private 38-image benchmark; verified CPU/CoreML parity and arm64 Docker inference without beginning the queued pipeline.

stages.title: Implement queued analysis pipeline
notes: Completed 2026-08-27: automatic canonical-asset dispatch now creates or reuses one logical FaceAnalysisRun and durably persists each attempt before raw SQS publication; the checksum-pinned Python worker uses service-audience signed GET and lifecycle-tagged write-once PUT authorities, independently verifies canonical bytes, enforces the 20-second/4 MiB bounds and emits reference-only completed/failed messages; Laravel's dedicated raw-SQS consumer resolves request_id through a SECURITY DEFINER trust bridge before tenant context, revalidates identity/current media state, checksum- and bounds-validates transient artifacts, persists immutable observations idempotently and deletes consumed artifacts. Three calibrated source queues have 30-second visibility, five-receive per-queue DLQs and least-privilege Terraform policies; scheduled five-minute staleness reconciliation retries with fresh attempts up to three; bounded reprocessing is audited; result artifacts have a one-day lifecycle backstop; and Family Space teardown includes face-analysis objects. Persistent PostgreSQL batch 33, a live ordinary-upload end-to-end proof, concurrent dispatch, poison-message, retry/redelivery, teardown, infrastructure and full repository gates passed without Phase 10 identity behavior.

stages.title: Add benchmark and operational metrics
notes: Completed 2026-08-27: the final direct private benchmark completed all 38 images with zero provider failures, 93 detections against 79 visible-face count annotations, 30 exact-count images, a 75/79 count-derived matched upper bound, four count-derived misses and 18 excess detections requiring review; hot CPU inference measured 69.569 ms median, 132.495 ms p95, 134.045 ms maximum, 13.068 sequential images/second and 973,864,960 bytes peak RSS. The production worker now emits trace-context-linked, low-cardinality OpenTelemetry for queue and end-to-end analysis latency, inference duration, attempts, completed/failed outcomes, bounded failure categories, detected/no-face counts, canonical dimensions, provider/model/configuration/backend identity and measurable peak memory without tenant identifiers, signed authorities or biometric values. The rebuilt stack, a real worker telemetry probe, complete repository, PostgreSQL 17.6, security, infrastructure and observability gates passed; Phase 9 completed without Phase 10 similarity, clustering, identity or review behavior.

stages.title: Accept face clustering and human identity review ADR
notes: ADR-0012 accepted 2026-08-28 (git tag phase-10-s01) after adversarial implementation-readiness reconciliation. The accepted architecture keeps PostgreSQL binary embeddings and provenance authoritative; uses checksum-verified, disposable pgvector projections behind a Fambam-owned tenant- and embedding-space-scoped abstraction; separates FaceIdentityAssignment from PhotoPerson with deterministic human-governed integration; provides durable suppression and recognition opt-out; keeps clusters identity-free, rebuildable and generation-scoped; integrates Person merge and guarded reversal; and gates automatic clustering and suggestions until S07 calibration acceptance. Stage scope was solely ADR acceptance, so the ADR-acceptance commit is the stage-completion commit.

stages.title: Implement embedding storage and similarity queries
notes: Completed 2026-08-28: provisioned pgvector-capable PostgreSQL 17 locally and in disposable regression infrastructure; added supporting tenant-consistent uniqueness for FaceObservation and Person plus the forced-RLS, checksum-bound, deterministically rebuildable face_embedding_projections table; projected new analysis results transactionally and existing observations through a tenant-bounded command without mutating authoritative bytea; introduced a Fambam-owned SimilaritySearch contract whose PostgreSQL adapter scopes by Family Space, projection version, dimension and full provider/model/weight/config identity. Persistent migration batch 34, bounded zero-row backfill, composite-FK/RLS, drift repair, incompatible-model, full repository, infrastructure, observability and security gates passed without beginning clustering.

stages.title: Implement conservative face clustering
notes: Completed 2026-08-28: added forced-RLS, tenant-consistent face-cluster generation/cluster/member persistence with database-enforced single-active-generation and single-active-membership invariants; implemented deterministic complete-link conservative clustering through the provider-neutral SimilaritySearch boundary; made building memberships non-operational and activation atomic with concurrent-generation revalidation; permanently protected human-retired membership history while allowing machine groupings to be reconsidered; extended Family Space teardown; and kept automatic processing disabled with no accepted numeric threshold until S07 calibration. Persistent migration batch 35, PostgreSQL lifecycle/RLS/composite-FK/teardown regressions and complete repository gates passed without beginning identity suggestion.

stages.title: Implement identity suggestion and confirmation
notes: Completed 2026-08-28: added the forced-RLS, tenant-consistent FaceIdentityAssignment lifecycle with database-enforced one-active-claim-per-face integrity and durable rejected/withdrawn history; extended the provider-neutral similarity boundary with approved trusted-gallery references; implemented gated strong/shortlist/none candidate generation with ambiguity and single-reference caution; implemented Member proposal and Owner/Administrator confirmation; and atomically ensured PhotoPerson through create, reuse-approved, resolve-pending and preserve-rejected-history transitions. Persistent migration batch 36, PostgreSQL gallery/RLS/composite-FK/partial-unique regressions and complete repository gates passed. All numeric recognition settings remain unset and automatic processing remains disabled until S07; suppression, cluster editing, consent and polished UI remain later-stage work.

stages.title: Implement merge, split, reject and unknown workflows
notes: Completed 2026-08-28: added forced-RLS, tenant-consistent durable FaceIdentitySuppression with audited reopening and filtering from automatic/manual reproposal; implemented active-current-generation cluster merge, split, Member naming proposal and Owner/Administrator confirmation while preserving inactive human-correction history and resolving identity only through FaceIdentityAssignment/PhotoPerson; extended Person merge snapshots, reconciliation and guarded reversal across assignments and suppressions, including capture, pending-to-withdrawn, then survivor-FK repointing with exact snapshot restoration. Persistent migration batch 37, focused correction/merge tests, PostgreSQL RLS/integrity regressions and complete repository gates passed without beginning recognition consent.

stages.title: Implement recognition consent and exclusion
notes: Completed 2026-08-28: added schema-level recognition_allowed NOT NULL DEFAULT false with automatic existing-Person backfill; implemented a dedicated Owner/Administrator consent endpoint whose opt-out transaction bulk-withdraws pending assignments and records one bundled audit while preserving approved assignments, PhotoPerson, observations and suppressions; excluded opted-out People at both the provider-neutral candidate boundary and PostgreSQL trusted-gallery query; preserved manual proposal and prevented re-enabling from resurrecting withdrawn suggestions. Persistent migration batch 38, consent/authorization/preservation tests, PostgreSQL gallery regression and complete repository gates passed without accepting calibration thresholds or enabling automatic processing.

stages.title: Calibrate against the family benchmark
notes: Completed 2026-08-28: expanded the private gitignored corpus to 79 images, 174 detected faces, 130 human-labelled faces, 20 anonymous identities and full ADR-0012 §16 coverage; added stable local annotation/import/validation and production-semantic leave-one-scene-out calibration tooling without persisting biometric values. Accepted profile buffalo-l-v0.7-private-family-v1 with clustering/strong cosine distance 0.350, shortlist 0.685, ambiguity margin 0.300 and two minimum strong references. Across 122 independent-scene trials it produced 33 correct and zero incorrect strong suggestions; complete-link clustering produced 26 correct and zero incorrect pairs. Thresholds are profile-bound and unknown profiles fail closed; the tracked processing default remains false, and the accepted profile was activated only through the separate private local operational setting. Phase 10 completed with recognition still opt-in and every identity decision human-confirmed.

delivery_log.description: FPA-P00-S01 completed: project definition and boundaries accepted.
FPA-P00-S02 completed: ADR-0001 accepted (repository and service topology). Stage scope was solely ADR acceptance, so the ADR commit is the stage-completion commit.
FPA-P00-S03 completed: repository foundation scaffold, documentation, command interface and initial CI integrated and verified.
Phase 0 completed: all Product and Repository Foundation stages and the full phase acceptance gate passed.

FPA-P01-S01 completed: ADR-0003 accepted (local development platform -- Docker Compose, LocalStack S3/SQS, Redis scoped to cache/state only, Phase 1 OpenTelemetry baseline). Stage scope was solely ADR acceptance, so the ADR commit is the stage-completion commit.
FPA-P01-S02 completed: React/Vite, Laravel and FastAPI applications scaffolded with independent health checks, tests and quality tooling.
FPA-P01-S03 completed: reproducible Docker Compose platform added with health-gated applications, PostgreSQL, Redis, LocalStack S3/SQS, Mailpit, persistent volumes and integration smoke checks.

FPA-P01-S04 completed: Phase 1 OpenTelemetry baseline added (instrumentation, Collector, Grafana otel-lgtm, HTTP/SQS trace-context propagation, structured logs). Phase-end review found and fixed a non-idempotent SQS smoke test and an unauthenticated debug endpoint; both confirmed resolved before completion.
Phase 1 completed: all Local Development Platform stages and the full phase acceptance gate passed.

FPA-P02-S01 completed: ADR-0004 accepted (identity, authentication and invitations -- headless Fortify with Sanctum SPA cookie sessions on a database session store, a shared global session/remember-me revocation operation, invitation-only account creation with the stock registration endpoint disabled, invitation acceptance treated as email verification, 15-character minimum password length with safeguarded HIBP screening, optional TOTP MFA, throttling instead of account lockout, no CAPTCHA or social login). Stage scope was solely ADR acceptance, so the ADR commit is the stage-completion commit.

FPA-P02-S02 completed: headless Fortify and Sanctum SPA cookie authentication, database sessions, login/logout, current-user profile, email-verification foundation and enumeration-safe password recovery implemented and verified. Open registration remains disabled pending FPA-P02-S03.

FPA-P02-S03 completed: first-account bootstrap, invitation issue/resend/revoke/expire/accept lifecycle, one-time fragment-token exchange, short-lived claims, verified account creation, audit coverage and feature-oriented TanStack Query frontend data access implemented and verified.

FPA-P02-S04 completed: shared global session/remember-token revocation, operator account revocation, consistent 15-to-255-character Argon2id-backed password policy with safeguarded HIBP screening, password-reset and account-security rate limiting, optional confirmed TOTP with one-time recovery-code disclosure, and typed feature-oriented frontend account-security/MFA surfaces implemented and verified. An independent review found and Codex corrected two blocking issues (a revoked account could complete an already-pending two-factor challenge and obtain a session; bcrypt silently truncated passwords beyond 72 bytes) and several important findings (repeatable plaintext recovery-code disclosure, unattributed operator revocation, a login timing side-channel, an insecure local secure-cookie example default); a focused re-review independently verified every fix, including a live reproduction confirming the revoked-mid-challenge exploit is now rejected.
Phase 2 completed: all Identity, Authentication and Invitations stages and the full phase acceptance gate passed, including an independent security review and its corrections.

FPA-P03-S01 completed: ADR-0005 accepted (family spaces and tenancy -- family_spaces/family_space_memberships tenant model with ULID identifiers and a mutable presentation slug; all five roadmap-named roles with a Phase 3 baseline meaning; family-space creation as a narrow platform-level capability never implied by any membership role or auto-granted at bootstrap; one invitation domain with atomic rejoin for removed members; friendly-URL resolution where unknown and inaccessible tenants are structurally indistinguishable and both return 404; at least one active Owner per space enforced at both the application and database-trigger layers; PostgreSQL RLS treated as three distinct policy classes -- tenant registry, access-control table, ordinary tenant-owned content tables -- to avoid a circular dependency between tenant resolution and tenant-scoped access control, with the exact policy implementation deliberately left to Phase 3 implementation rather than frozen in the ADR). Stage scope was solely ADR acceptance, so the ADR commit is the stage-completion commit.

FPA-P03-S02 completed: Family Space and membership foundations, capability-gated creation, Owner safeguards at application and deferred PostgreSQL constraint layers, family-scoped invitations and atomic existing-account membership reactivation implemented and verified. The approved persistent migration backfilled the fallback Family Archive and memberships, associated historical invitations, expired pending Phase 2 invitations, removed their claims and retired can_invite.

FPA-P03-S03 completed: active-membership slug resolution, request-scoped tenant context, role policies, explicit tenant query scoping, nested Family Space routes and protected URL-derived React routing implemented and verified. Unknown and inaccessible Family Spaces return the same 404, out-of-role members receive 403 only after resolution, cross-tenant nested identifiers fail closed and tenant context is cleared after dispatch.

FPA-P03-S04 completed: a separately provisioned non-superuser, non-BYPASSRLS runtime role, transaction-local actor and tenant context, forced PostgreSQL RLS policies for the tenant registry and membership access-control table, and the reusable fail-closed ordinary tenant-table policy pattern were implemented and verified. PostgreSQL 17.6 tests directly proved non-recursive registry resolution, cross-tenant read/write isolation, atomic authoritative flows and context cleanup; the approved persistent migration and rebuilt-stack verification preserved existing tenant data and passed all smoke gates.

FPA-P03-S05 completed: tenant-aware audit records, explicit asynchronous tenant/actor/correlation/trace propagation, safe Family Space storage partitioning, an isolated Laravel job queue and the Owner-controlled deletion lifecycle were implemented and verified. The accepted follow-up review added direct PostgreSQL concurrency, multi-space cross-tenant and insert-only audit-boundary proof plus frontend route, cache-isolation and membership-loss regressions.
Phase 3 completed: all Family Spaces and Tenancy stages passed the full repository, PostgreSQL 17.6, persistent migration, rebuilt-stack and independent review acceptance gates.

FPA-P04-S01 completed: ADR-0006 accepted (people, accounts and relationships -- Family-Space-local Person identity with no cross-tenant matching; immutable ULID Person identity with mutable names, a shared uncertain-date concept, and an independently-composed deceased state; a proposed-versus-authoritative distinction applied uniformly to Person details and relationships, with proposed relationships excluded from the authoritative graph until Owner/Administrator approval and approval re-validating against current state; one-to-one User-to-Person linking per Family Space with Member/Contributor self-claim proposals; one canonical relationship edge per concept with derived inverse wording; People-only, presentation-only Family Circles barred from ever affecting authorization; a Phase 4 visibility baseline giving Owner/Administrator/Member default Person access and none to Contributor/Guest; full Class C tenancy inheritance from ADR-0005; Person merge via redirect/tombstone with structured provenance and realistically bounded reversal; and ULID-only Person routes). Stage scope was solely ADR acceptance, so the ADR-acceptance commit is the stage-completion commit.

FPA-P04-S02 completed: Family-Space-local ULID Person records, normalized uncertain dates, independent deceased state, bounded shared biography, provisional Member creation, Owner/Administrator authoritative writes and bounded detail-proposal review, whole-record role visibility, tenant-aware audit events, forced Class C RLS and a feature-oriented TanStack Query frontend were implemented, persistently migrated and verified.

FPA-P04-S03 completed: database-enforced one-to-one account links, bounded Member self-claims with the future reachable-Contributor permission ceiling preserved without a guessed-ULID bypass, Owner/Administrator approval, correction and removal, access-loss retention, complete audit coverage, forced Class C RLS and typed TanStack Query Person-page controls were implemented, persistently migrated and verified.

FPA-P04-S04 completed: canonical relationships with current-state validation, Member proposals, Owner/Administrator authoritative resolution, flat presentation-only Family Circles, distinct audits, forced Class C RLS and typed TanStack Query frontend flows were implemented, persistently migrated and verified.

FPA-P04-S05 completed: duplicate proposals, immutable-ULID tombstone redirects, atomic Phase-4 reference reconciliation, structured merge provenance, bounded exact-state reversal with manual-correction refusal, complete audits, forced Class C RLS and typed TanStack Query frontend controls were implemented, persistently migrated and verified.
Phase 4 completed: all People, Accounts and Relationships stages passed the full repository, PostgreSQL 17.6, persistent migration and rebuilt-stack acceptance gates.

FPA-P05-S01 completed: ADR-0007 accepted. Phase 5 owns MediaUpload and MediaVariant infrastructure independently of Phase 6 Photo records; direct upload uses tenant-scoped extension-independent staging, server-detected final keys and a verified write-once-equivalent boundary; preserved originals remain byte-for-byte immutable with SHA-256 integrity and complete metadata; Laravel owns deterministic validation, required configurable malware scanning, canonical generation and fixed variants across JPEG, PNG, HEIC/HEIF, WebP and TIFF; ordinary presentation withholds privacy-sensitive metadata while authorised original downloads return the untouched file; Contributor upload remains a Phase 6/7 resource-scoped placeholder; and ADR-0005 tenant deletion is the sole preserved-media deletion exception. Stage scope was solely ADR acceptance, so this ADR-acceptance commit is the stage-completion commit.

FPA-P05-S02 completed: tenant-isolated MediaUpload persistence, role-bounded and idempotent initiation, extension-independent staging keys, signed conditional direct-upload authority, independently inspected and duplicate-safe completion, tenant/correlation/trace context, audit coverage, LocalStack browser integration and a typed feature-local TanStack Query upload flow were implemented, persistently migrated and verified. Validation, malware scanning and archival finalisation remain FPA-P05-S03.

FPA-P05-S03 completed: tenant-aware validation jobs, signature-derived accepted-format detection, bounded decoding, server-computed SHA-256, fail-closed replaceable ClamAV scanning, write-once archival and quarantine finalisation, durable audits and staging cleanup, and narrowly discoverable seven-day quarantine retention were implemented, persistently migrated and verified with real decoder, EICAR, LocalStack and PostgreSQL RLS coverage.

FPA-P05-S04 completed: source-integrity-bound tenant jobs, private normalized metadata and lossless raw EXIF/ICC extraction, GPS withholding, deterministic auto-oriented sRGB metadata-stripped JPEG/PNG canonical generation, immutable canonical finalisation and the preserved-to-processing transition were implemented, persistently migrated and verified across HEIC, HEIF, TIFF, transparency, PostgreSQL RLS and real LocalStack storage.

FPA-P05-S05 completed: the fixed thumbnail, card and display variant set; metadata-stripped sRGB WebP generation with transparency preservation; versioned MediaVariant identity; unique tenant-aware jobs; canonical-integrity verification; write-once and database idempotency; ready/degraded transitions; disposable regeneration; persistent migration; real ImageMagick processing; LocalStack storage; observability; and PostgreSQL Class C isolation were implemented and verified.

FPA-P05-S06 completed: tenant- and role-authorized canonical, fixed-variant and preserved-original authority endpoints; bounded key-scoped signed GETs; verified response MIME types and Range support; explicit private-bucket, browser CORS and signature-validation controls; fail-closed unavailable and cross-tenant behaviour; and truthful original_download_authorised auditing were implemented and verified with role/state regressions, real LocalStack delivery, observability and PostgreSQL tenancy gates.

FPA-P05-S07 completed: source-bound duplicate-safe degraded recovery with Owner/Administrator orphan recovery; independent per-file bulk upload with typed TanStack Query progress, partial-failure and processing-retry controls; narrowly executable 24-hour abandoned-upload discovery and retryable staging cleanup; and idempotent, paginated tenant media-prefix and Phase-5-row teardown were implemented, persistently migrated and verified.

Phase 5 completed: the Media Storage and Upload Pipeline passed the complete repository, PostgreSQL 17.6, persistent migration, real format-processing, malware-validation, LocalStack storage/delivery/teardown, observability and security acceptance gates.

FPA-P06-S01 completed: ADR-0008 accepted. Photo.media_upload_id is required, unique and one-directional to MediaUpload; Photo.created_by is distinct from and authority-bearing over MediaUpload.user_id. Photographer, scanner and original physical owner are single-valued, Person-or-free-text provenance roles following ADR-0006's proposed/authoritative pattern; historical date reuses ADR-0006's uncertain-date concept and stays separate from EXIF capture timestamps. PhotoPerson uses the same proposed/authoritative pattern and is never overwritten by future machine recognition. Photo visibility is family_space or private only; selected-audience sharing lives entirely in Albums via AlbumGrant, with explicit, tested, reversible visibility widening on Album addition/removal. Default family_space Album contribution is fixed as product policy for Owner/Administrator/creator/Member, with Contributor gated behind an explicit AlbumGrant as its first concrete resource-scoped role. Phase 5's delivery endpoints must become Photo/Album-aware so the MediaUpload ULID cannot bypass private or restricted access. Photo deletion is reversible soft deletion only, scoped to Owner/Administrator and the Photo's creator. Stage scope was solely ADR acceptance, so this ADR-acceptance commit is the stage-completion commit.

FPA-P06-S02 completed: tenant-isolated Photo, identity-bearing provenance proposal and Family-Space tag records; role-bounded promotion of ready MediaUploads; intrinsic Photo visibility enforced through existing canonical, variant and original delivery routes; Person merge reconciliation and exact reversal; Family Space teardown integration; and typed feature-local TanStack Query list, detail, editing, tag and provenance flows were implemented, persistently migrated and verified.

FPA-P06-S03 completed: Photo historical dates reuse the exact ADR-0006 uncertain-date contract while remaining independent of EXIF; human-supplied free-text location remains independent of GPS; retained PhotoPerson proposals expose only confirmed associations as human ground truth; Member proposal and Owner/Administrator resolution, audit, Person merge and exact reversal, forced Class C RLS and typed feature-local TanStack Query controls were implemented, persistently migrated and verified.

FPA-P06-S04 completed: tenant-isolated Albums, ordered AlbumPhoto membership and membership-scoped AlbumGrant records; live Private, Selected and Family Space authorization; explicit and reversible private-Photo widening; Contributor upload strictly through a live can_contribute grant; Album-aware presentation delivery; query-only dynamic filters; and typed feature-local TanStack Query UI were implemented, persistently migrated and verified.

FPA-P06-S05 completed: attributed Photo stories and comments with author editing, durable revisions and moderated soft removal; one-per-user fixed-vocabulary reactions without ranking or feed behaviour; audit trails; and typed feature-local TanStack Query UI were implemented, persistently migrated and verified.

FPA-P06-S06 completed: reversible tenant-isolated Photo soft deletion and restoration; authority based on Photo.created_by rather than MediaUpload.user_id; retention of Album, story, comment, reaction and Phase 5 asset records; complete presentation and asset-delivery denial while deleted; association-preserving restoration; and ADR-0005-only permanent tenant teardown were implemented, persistently migrated and verified.

Phase 6 completed: the Photo Domain, Provenance and Organisation passed the complete repository, frontend, API, PostgreSQL 17.6 RLS, persistent migration, asset-delivery, contracts and security acceptance gates.

FPA-P07-S01 completed: ADR-0009 accepted. Event, Event-linked Albums, explicit primary-Event provenance, derived attendance, deterministic invitation/admission reuse, live revocable Guest admission, Album-level Guest participation, the narrow Event original-download exception, split conversational versus Story authority, reversible Event removal and advisory duplicate review were architecturally fixed before implementation. Stage scope was solely ADR acceptance, so this ADR-acceptance commit is the stage-completion commit.

FPA-P07-S02 completed: tenant-isolated Event records, creator/manager editing, authorization-inert Event links from Albums and Photos, confirmed-PhotoPerson-derived attendance, Person reverse lookup, deterministic advisory duplicate candidates, typed TanStack Query Event and Event-Album UI, persistent PostgreSQL migration, database constraints and forced RLS were implemented and verified.

FPA-P07-S03 completed: Event Albums were verified to reuse the existing Member and grant-scoped Contributor contribution paths, including MediaUpload.target_album_id finalisation to one private attached Photo, without introducing Guest admission or participation behaviour from S04.

FPA-P07-S04 completed: restricted authenticated Guest access now composes an active Guest membership, a live EventAdmission and Album guest_participation or an Event-scoped individual grant; Event invitations reuse existing memberships without role mutation; Guests remain excluded from ordinary Family Space surfaces; uploads reuse the existing Album-targeted pipeline; original download remains participation-scoped; comments/reactions are separated from denied Guest Story authoring; and Event removal/restoration disables/resumes access without destroying references.

FPA-P07-S05 completed: retry-safe, deduplicated Event-contribution notifications delivered through a tenant-scoped per-recipient ledger; bounded, overlap-protected curated Event archive generation with checksum-validated originals, a schema-versioned manifest, signed downloads, retention and idempotent expiry cleanup; and closure of the independent Phase 7 review findings (Guest-created-Photo authority tied to live Event access, race-safe concurrent Event-invitation acceptance, correct Album event-detachment guest_participation reset, consistent Event date-range validation against stored state, and direct event_admissions RLS proof), all verified with full API, PostgreSQL 17.6, frontend, security, infrastructure and observability gates.
Phase 7 completed: Events and Collaborative Sharing passed the complete repository, PostgreSQL 17.6, persistent migration, frontend, security, infrastructure and observability acceptance gates.

FPA-P08-S01 completed: ADR-0010 accepted. Exact and perceptual duplicate detection remain advisory, tenant-isolated and visibility-filtered; the three-outcome choice is mapped onto both Photo-creation paths without changing promotion authority; existing conversation history is preserved while new conversation becomes Album-scoped; duplicate decisions suppress automatic rediscovery with explicit audited reopening; and Phase 8 introduces no merge, redirect, aggregation, consolidation or automatic deletion mechanism.

FPA-P08-S02 completed: tenant- and visibility-scoped exact SHA-256 detection across direct Photo creation and asynchronous Album/Event contribution; deterministic three-outcome resolution and uploader-owned duplicate holds; canonical multi-match DuplicateDecision suppression; idempotent retrospective exact candidates; Album-scoped new comments and reactions with preserved read-only legacy history; typed TanStack Query UI; persistent PostgreSQL migration; and forced RLS were implemented and verified.
